items.title: Addy Osmani 谈 Agent 时代如何保持批判性思维
items.description: Addy Osmani 发文探讨在大量使用 Agent 工作流后如何保持批判性思维。他提出认知卸载、拖延、认知投降三段光谱，认为模型越强、输出越流畅，人越容易在不知不觉中放弃独立判断；并给出具体做法，包括提问前先写假设、把验证标准前置为可执行测试、要求 Agent 列出它替你做的决策与假设、用测验收尾而不是读摘要，以及定期手写代码做校准练习。他强调可以卸载工作和审计，但不能卸载责任。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/uinaiwkzg4u2exkfgv4oha9p7

items.title: 云存储服务提供商 Dropbox 计划收购 Tigris Data，拓展企业开发者 AI 存储服务

items.content: 比如，一个第三方平台声称接入了旗舰模型，后台却换成便宜的小模型、旧模型，光看回答的语气和质量，我们很难判断；又或者是同一道题目，官网能做出来，用中转站却卡住了。 一个看起来简单的模型请求，背后需要经过「用户—中转站—上游服务商—模型」多个环节，只要其中一环缺少透明度，我们就很难确认自己买到的，是不是标价对应的模型。 这套名为 FlashProve 的开源研究原型，可以为模型推理生成密码学证明。它尝试让服务商为模型的计算结果提供密码学证明，用户不用拿到模型权重，也不用自己再跑一遍大模型，就能核验。 除了使用模型厂商官方的应用，和从官网调用 API 进行对话，我们能确认使用模型的情况。在大多数的 API 调用里，我们提交问题，服务器返回回答，模型世界上是跑在了远程的机器上，我们无法得知后台究竟进行了那些计算。 斯坦福大学的研究项目《Model Equality Testing》曾经就测试过 2024 年四款 Llama 模型的 31 个商业 API 端点，发现其中 11 个端点的输出分布，与 Meta 发布权重的参考分布存在统计差异。 同一个模型名字，有时候并不能对应同一种表现。即便在服务页面挂着的都是 Opus 5.5，但根本无法保证用户获得完全相同的模型。

Hardware startup Aina released a smart ring today that features a screen, a joystick, and a mic so that you can talk to your agents and take notes. The $399 ring has a speaker so you can take calls using it as well. The startup, which raised $5.5 million in July , is positioning the ring as a controller of sorts for both AI and non-AI apps. The company previously made Mirage, a three-key controller that let you invoke buttons based on the app on your Mac’s screen. For instance, if you were on a Google Meet call, you could map keys to camera on/off, mic mute/unmute, or to leave the meeting. Aina has baked in lessons from that device to create the new ring, which it’s simply calling “AI ring.” Using its mic, you can take notes, send a prompt to agents, set reminders, and dictate notes on your Mac using Wispr Flow or the startup’s own dictation engine.

items.description: Discovered Materials, a months-old YC startup that uses AI to find chip materials, is offering $200,000 for each solution to five open materials science problems.
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Discovered Materials, a months-old, San Francisco startup using AI models to find new substances for building advanced chips, announced a million-dollar challenge for AI models to solve five critical problems in materials science. While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials. “It’s more difficult to specify problems clearly in materials science because it’s not like math, where you have a very specific definition and can get to a yes or no,” said Advaith Sridhar, a co-founder of Discovered Materials, which was part of Y Combinator’s spring 2026 batch. “We came to this discussion [wondering], what are the grand challenges in this field? How do we know AI is making progress?” Though materials science doesn’t have an equivalent of the Millennium Prize Problems, Discovered Materials recruited an advisory group of academics at leading global universities to spell out five open problems. The company is offering a pool of prizes, worth $1 million in total, for solutions to the problems.

items.content: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE. Almost a year ago to the day, Figure AI CEO Brett Adcock responded to some gentle social media taunting from rival robotics company Agility with a prediction: “You’ll be bankrupt in <12 months.” Instead, Agility is going public through a reverse-merger that will see it become a publicly-traded company and raise $465 million in new capital from retail investors and a tranche of private funding. The transaction will take place through a special purpose acquisition company, or SPAC. “You don’t see a lot of dancing robots or backflipping robots from Agility,” CEO Peggy Johnson told TechCrunch ahead of the company’s market debut. “We stuck to our strategy, which [are] these manual, very repetitive jobs, that it’s hard to find humans to do.” Agility predates the recent boom in physical AI investment. The company was spun out of Oregon State University in 2015 by a group of researchers who made headway in figuring out how to get a robot to walk safely on two legs. The company has focused on deploying a handful of its Digit robots in industrial settings with nine different customers, including Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre. Digits are generally used to move heavy totes, including more than 100,000 of them at a GXO logistics facility.
